subject: Cutting back a spent broad bean
prompt: Generate a single strictly SQUARE 1:1, full-bleed, high-resolution documentary photograph for page 149 of The Vegetable Guru, a small print panel. It is a square re-composition of the first image, which the author liked: keep the same up-close documentary moment, working dark crumbly soil, an old brick finger-path edge at the lower left, single right bare working hand entering from the right with plain dark cuff and worn small dark-red-handled bypass secateurs, and a spent broad bean stem being snipped at soil level with the roots left firmly in the soil. Treat it as widening the existing camera framing to either side rather than backing away from the teaching detail. Keep the subject nearly as large and clear, the primary stem just left of the centre, with its green base visibly entering the soil, and the curved metal cutting blade and opposing counterblade plausibly closing on opposite sides of the same stem 5–12 mm above ground. One small already-cut stub naturally just behind. Show one or two additional distinct, mature broad bean plants on each side, rooting into the same bed, separated from the focus by shallow depth of field. Their stems may partly enter frame upwards, with a few older leaves and subdued remaining Vicia faba pods near the top and outer edges; allow natural variation in stem spacing, heights and foliage. Keep the working hand and secateurs unobstructed in the centre and lower centre, preserve distinct hand anatomy, and do not create copies of the central stem. The other photos are role-specific reference only: the second is the real low brick-path perspective at John's Cornish allotment, the third is a real view of how his earth beds and paths sit, and the fourth is his own broad bean foliage and pods for real anatomy. Keep incidental plot background short, subdued and authentic. Suitable diffuse natural daylight, no uprooted plant, visible roots, labels, frames, person’s head, gloves, added garden buildings, landscaping or excessive foreground clutter. Exact square, no white margin.
